codes.name: repetition d=5
codes.description: Qubits in a row; each check compares two neighbours (Z_i Z_i+1). Catches bit flips (X) only - a single Z flip is a logical error, so as a quantum code d = 1, but against X errors the distance is d.
references: Nielsen & Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information, ch. 10 (sec. 10.1)

written.title: Stabilizer generators
written.text: Each line is one check: the Pauli it measures on each qubit (qubit numbers as on the lattice).
written.pre:
S0   (Z    )  Z0 Z1
S1   (Z    )  Z1 Z2
S2   (Z    )  Z2 Z3
S3   (Z    )  Z3 Z4

written.title: Check matrices (0/1)
written.text: CSS code: X checks and Z checks are separate 0/1 matrices. Row = check, column = qubit, 1 = the check looks at that qubit. They commute exactly when H_X · H_Zᵀ = 0 (mod 2).

written.title: Polynomial form
written.text: A cyclic-style code: every check is the same pattern (1 1) shifted one qubit along the line.
written.pre:
check polynomial h(x) = 1 + x
row i of H_Z = xⁱ·(1 + x)   for i = 0 … 3
(no X checks: a single Z flip goes unseen, so d_Z = 1, while d_X = 5)

codes.d_how: 1 as a quantum code (no check sees a Z flip); 5 against bit flips (Stim, exact)

codes.name: Shor [[9,1,3]]
codes.description: Three blocks of three (rows). Inside a row, pairwise Z checks catch a bit flip (3-qubit repetition code). Across two rows, a six-qubit X check compares the phase of the blocks, catching a phase flip. Degenerate: Z0 and Z1 have the same syndrome and either correction works.
references: Nielsen & Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information, ch. 10 (sec. 10.2)

written.title: Stabilizer generators

S2   (Z    )  Z0 Z1
S3   (Z    )  Z1 Z2
S4   (Z    )  Z3 Z4
S5   (Z    )  Z4 Z5
S6   (Z    )  Z6 Z7
S7   (Z    )  Z7 Z8

written.title: Check matrices (0/1)
written.text: CSS code: X checks and Z checks are separate 0/1 matrices. Row = check, column = qubit, 1 = the check looks at that qubit. They commute exactly when H_X · H_Zᵀ = 0 (mod 2).

written.title: Algebraic form
written.text: Shor's code is a concatenation: an outer 3-qubit phase-flip code whose 'qubits' are 3-qubit bit-flip blocks. No polynomial; its structure is a product.
written.pre:
|0_L> = (|000> + |111>)⊗3,  |1_L> = (|000> − |111>)⊗3
inner (per row): Z0Z1, Z1Z2   outer (across rows): X on rows 0+1, X on rows 1+2

codes.d_how: exact (brute force over all small errors)

codes.name: Steane [[7,1,3]]
codes.description: Seven qubits on a triangle with three four-qubit faces. Each face is measured twice, once as XXXX and once as ZZZZ. The three faces are the parity checks of the classical Hamming [7,4,3] code, so every single error gives a different pattern of faces. This is the smallest 2D colour code.
references: Bombin & Martin-Delgado, Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 180501 (2006) (colour codes)

S3   (Z    )  Z0 Z1 Z3 Z4
S4   (Z    )  Z1 Z2 Z4 Z5
S5   (Z    )  Z3 Z4 Z5 Z6

written.title: Check matrices (0/1)
written.text: CSS code: X checks and Z checks are separate 0/1 matrices. Row = check, column = qubit, 1 = the check looks at that qubit. They commute exactly when H_X · H_Zᵀ = 0 (mod 2).

written.title: Algebraic form
written.text: Steane = CSS(Hamming, Hamming): both H_X and H_Z are the [7,4,3] Hamming checks. Hamming is a cyclic code with generator g(x) = 1 + x + x³ when the qubits are numbered around a cycle (this drawing uses the triangle numbering instead).
written.pre:
Hamming checks: column j = binary of the face set qubit j belongs to
every non-zero 3-bit pattern appears exactly once -> every single error has its own syndrome

codes.name: five-qubit [[5,1,3]]
codes.description: Five qubits on a ring. One stabilizer, XZZXI, is shifted one step around the ring four times. It mixes X and Z in the same check, so it is not CSS. It is the smallest code that corrects any single-qubit error, and it is 'perfect': the 15 single errors plus 'no error' use up all 2^4 = 16 syndromes exactly.

written.title: Stabilizer generators
written.text: Each line is one check: the Pauli it measures on each qubit (qubit numbers as on the lattice).
written.pre:
S0   (mixed)  X0 Z1 Z2 X3
S1   (mixed)  X1 Z2 Z3 X4
S2   (mixed)  X0 X2 Z3 Z4
S3   (mixed)  Z0 X1 X3 Z4

written.title: Check matrices (0/1)
written.text: Not CSS, so each check is a pair of 0/1 rows: its X part and its Z part (both 1 = Y). Two checks commute when x₁·z₂ + z₁·x₂ = 0 (mod 2).

written.title: Polynomial form
written.text: A cyclic code over 5 qubits. Write the X part and Z part of the first check as polynomials in x (x = shift by one qubit, x⁵ = 1); the other checks are x, x², x³ times it.
written.pre:
first check XZZXI:
  X part a(x) = 1 + x³
  Z part b(x) = x + x²
check k = ( xᵏ a(x) | xᵏ b(x) )  mod (x⁵ − 1),  k = 0 … 3
(the 5th shift is the product of the other four, so only 4 are independent)

codes.name: surface (unrotated) d=3
codes.description: Kitaev's surface code with boundaries. Qubits sit on the edges of a square grid. X checks sit on vertices (the star of 4 edges) and Z checks on faces (the 4 edges around a square). A logical X is a string of X's crossing the grid; any shorter string leaves two lit checks at its ends.
references: Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl, Preskill, J. Math. Phys. 43, 4452 (2002)

codes.name: toric 4x4
codes.description: The surface code with opposite edges glued together (a torus), so there is no boundary. Every check has 4 qubits. Two logical qubits, from the two independent ways a string can wrap around the torus. One X check and one Z check are redundant: the product of all X checks is the identity.
references: Dennis et al., J. Math. Phys. 43, 4452 (2002)

written.title: Stabilizer generators
written.text: Each line is one check: the Pauli it measures on each qubit (qubit numbers as on the lattice).

written.title: Check matrices (0/1)
written.text: CSS code: X checks and Z checks are separate 0/1 matrices. Row = check, column = qubit, 1 = the check looks at that qubit. They commute exactly when H_X · H_Zᵀ = 0 (mod 2).

written.title: Polynomial form
written.text: Each term xᵃyᵇ is one arrow: a check touches the qubit a cells away along x and b cells away along y (which way round is a labelling choice). The same arrows repeat in every cell, which is why one term is one full CNOT layer in the circuit.
written.pre:
torus: l = 4, m = 4   (16 cells, each with an L qubit, an R qubit, an X check, a Z check)
x = cyclic shift by one cell along the l direction  (16 x 16 permutation matrix)
y = cyclic shift by one cell along the m direction

A = 1 + x
B = 1 + y

H_X = [ A | B ]        (X check at cell c: L qubits c·A, R qubits c·B)
H_Z = [ Bᵀ | Aᵀ ]

Why they commute: H_X H_Zᵀ = A B + B A = 0 (mod 2), because x and y commute.

replays.title: MWPM fixes a weight-3 chain (surface d=5)
replays.caption: Three X errors light Z checks at the two ends of the chain. Matching pairs the lit checks along the shortest path, so the correction is the same chain.

replays.title: MWPM loses to 3 errors down a column (surface d=5)
replays.caption: Three X errors from the top edge: only one check lights, at the bottom of the chain. Going to the far boundary costs 2, back to the near one costs 3, so matching picks the far side - error + correction spans the code: logical error. A distance-5 code fixes at most 2 errors.

replays.title: Three errors that are really one (surface d=5)
replays.caption: X on qubits 0, 1, 2 lights a single check. Qubits 1 and 2 together are a weight-2 boundary stabilizer, so this error is equivalent to X on qubit 0 alone. Matching corrects qubit 0 and the code is fine: degeneracy you can see.

replays.title: BP stuck on a tie (toric 4x4)
replays.caption: Two lit checks on a diagonal: two equally short corrections. BP gives all four qubits the same probability and never chooses (degeneracy).

replays.title: BP converges (gross code)
replays.caption: A weight-4 error: the probability gathers on the true error and every check is satisfied.

replays.title: BP oscillates (gross code)
replays.caption: Also weight 4 - well inside the distance 12 - but BP never settles: short loops in the Tanner graph make its beliefs flip back and forth. This is why the gross code is decoded with BP+OSD or Relay-BP.
